name: HubSpot
summary: HubSpot OAuth is self-serve and fast: any standard HubSpot account can now build a project-based app with the hs CLI, get a client ID/secret, and mint 30-minute access tokens with refresh tokens in under an hour, with no review unless you want an App Marketplace listing. The real traps are scope/tier gating (an install fails outright if the target portal's tier lacks a required scope), the 110-requests-per-10-seconds per-portal limit, and the fact that legacy public apps can no longer be created since June 23, 2026 so every new integration must use the projects-based developer platform.

composio.note: HubSpot (HUBSPOT) is listed under Composio-managed auth, so you can skip app registration entirely. If you bring your own app, register https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback as a redirect URL and set the same value as oauth_redirect_uri in the Composio auth config.

verdict.difficultyReason: No approval gate for private/allowlisted distribution; the only friction is installing the HubSpot CLI, declaring scopes in app-hsmeta.json, and understanding which scopes are tier-gated. Marketplace listing adds a 10-business-day review and a 3-active-install minimum, but is optional.

approvalWait.note: Zero wait for private or allowlisted OAuth distribution. Only an App Marketplace listing is reviewed: initial review within 10 business days, full feedback loop capped at 60 days. Certification (optional, after 6 months listed and 60 installs) is a separate 10-business-day review.

verdict.timeToFirstToken: Under 1 hour (CLI install + project upload + test-account install)

prerequisites.text: A HubSpot account where you are a Super Admin (free tier works). As of March 9, 2026 legacy app developer accounts were migrated into standard accounts, so a separate developer account is no longer required; the Development menu exists in every standard account.

Node.js and the HubSpot CLI (npm install -g @hubspot/cli@latest, docs reference v7.6.0+), authenticated with hs account auth. New apps can only be created as projects; legacy public app creation ended June 23, 2026.
An HTTPS redirect URL on a real domain (http://localhost is allowed for testing; IP addresses are rejected).
A developer test account (up to 10 per account, free, 90-day Enterprise trial) to install into without touching production data.
For Marketplace listing only: public setup docs, Terms of Service URL, Privacy Policy URL, support contact, and acceptance of the Technology Partner Program Agreement.

steps.title: Sign in to a HubSpot account as Super Admin
steps.detail: Create or sign in to a standard HubSpot account (free is fine). Since March 9, 2026 there is no separate app developer account; the Development section in any standard account is where apps, projects, and test accounts live.
tips: Only Super Admins (or users with Marketplace Access) can install apps, so the installing human needs that role in the target portal.

steps.title: Create a developer test account
steps.detail: Go to Development > Testing > Test Accounts and click Create developer test account. Each standard account can hold up to 10; they ship with a 90-day Enterprise-feature trial and expire after 90 days with no API calls (renewable up to 30 days before expiry).
tips: Enterprise trial means tier-gated scopes (custom objects, automation) will install here but may fail in a customer's Starter portal; test with the Customize my test account option to simulate lower tiers.

steps.title: Install and authenticate the HubSpot CLI
steps.detail: Run npm install -g @hubspot/cli@latest then hs account auth, which opens a browser to generate a personal access key for the account. The CLI is the only way to create a non-legacy app.
tips: An agent can run the npm install and prepare the command, but the personal-access-key generation requires an authenticated browser session.

steps.title: Scaffold the app project with hs project create
steps.detail: Run hs project create, choose App, then answer prompts for distribution (Marketplace vs private/allowlisted) and authentication (OAuth vs static token). This generates hsproject.json (platformVersion 2026.09) and app-hsmeta.json.
tips: Choose auth.type oauth even for an internal tool if you will install into more than one portal; static auth is single-account only.

steps.title: Declare redirect URLs and scopes in app-hsmeta.json
steps.detail: In the auth block set redirectUrls (HTTPS required, http://localhost allowed), requiredScopes (at least one, and at least one read scope such as crm.objects.contacts.read), optionalScopes, and conditionallyRequiredScopes. Set distribution to marketplace or private.
tips: Put tier-gated scopes (automation, content, crm.objects.custom.*) in optionalScopes or conditionallyRequiredScopes, never requiredScopes, or installs will fail on lower-tier portals.
For Composio bring-your-own auth add https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback to redirectUrls.

steps.title: Upload the project and read the client ID/secret
steps.detail: Run hs project upload to build and deploy, then hs project open. Under Project Components click the app UID, open the Auth tab, and copy the Client ID and Client secret into your OAuth server config.
tips: Any later scope or redirect change is made by editing app-hsmeta.json and re-running hs project upload; the UI is read-only for project-defined features.

steps.title: Install the app into the test account
steps.detail: In the app's Distribution tab click Add test install(s), pick the test account, review scopes, tick the box acknowledging an unverified app, and click Connect app. Alternatively build the install URL https://app.hubspot.com/oauth/authorize?client_id=...&scope=...&optional_scope=...&redirect_uri=... and open it as a Super Admin.
tips: Every scope in requiredScopes must appear in the scope query parameter or HubSpot shows an authorization-page error.

steps.title: Exchange the code for tokens and implement refresh
steps.detail: POST form-encoded grant_type=authorization_code, client_id, client_secret, redirect_uri, code to https://api.hubapi.com/oauth/v3/token (legacy apps use /oauth/v1/token). The response has access_token, refresh_token, and expires_in=1800. Refresh with grant_type=refresh_token before the 30 minutes elapse.
tips: Inspect the returned token's scopes: optional scopes the portal lacked are silently dropped and you must handle their absence at runtime.

steps.title: Verify your domain to remove the unverified-app install warning
steps.detail: Add the TXT record HubSpot gives you for the app's domain (one verified domain per account, shared by all its apps). DNS propagation can take up to 48 hours; removing the record brings the warning back. Marketplace-listed apps skip this step.

steps.title: Optional: submit an App Marketplace listing
steps.detail: Only needed for public discovery. Requires OAuth as the sole auth method, at least 3 active unique installs from unaffiliated production accounts with activity in the last 30 days, live setup/support/ToS/privacy URLs, no sensitive-data scopes, and a supported platform version. Initial review takes up to 10 business days; the whole loop is capped at 60 days; only one app may be under review at a time.
tips: AI-connector apps must require user-level permissions (2026.09) or be built on HubSpot's MCP Server to be listable.

scopes.note: Scopes are declared in app-hsmeta.json as requiredScopes, optionalScopes, or conditionallyRequiredScopes and requested via the scope / optional_scope query parameters. No scope needs HubSpot approval, but many are gated by the installing portal's product tier: a required scope the portal cannot grant makes the install fail with an error, while an optional scope is silently dropped. Tokens carry the app's scopes, not the installing user's permissions. Legacy scopes (tickets, files, hubdb, timeline) still work but granular ones are recommended; sensitive-data scopes are Enterprise-only and disqualify an app from Marketplace listing.

examples.purpose: Baseline scope added to every OAuth app; required for token exchange
Read contact records and properties (any tier)
Create, edit, and delete deals (any tier)
Read custom objects; Enterprise portals only, so keep it optional/conditional
Workflows API; requires Marketing Hub Professional or Enterprise
Pages, blog, email, campaigns; requires CMS or Marketing Hub Professional/Enterprise
Read one-to-one sales email content (any tier)
Sensitive contact properties; Enterprise-only and blocks Marketplace listing

triggers: Submitting an App Marketplace listing (distribution: marketplace)
Applying for App Certification after the listing has been live 6 months
Building an AI-connector app for the Marketplace (must use user-level permissions or HubSpot MCP Server)
approval.process: Private/allowlisted OAuth apps need no review: upload the project and install. For a Marketplace listing, build the listing in the account's Marketplace provider area and submit; HubSpot's Ecosystem Quality team manually reviews it, sends feedback if anything is incomplete or misleading, and publishes or rejects. Only one app can be in review at a time. Certification is a separate later request requiring 60 active installs, a 95% API success rate, a demo video of the uninstall flow, and a security questionnaire; it is valid for two years.
approval.reviewTime: Official: initial listing review within 10 business days, full review-and-feedback loop no more than 60 days from when feedback is shared; certification responses also within 10 business days. Community-observed: most listings clear in 1-3 weeks when the URLs and scope table are accurate (inferred; not confirmed in official docs).
reviewerAsksFor: At least 3 active, unique installs from production accounts unaffiliated with your organization (activity within 30 days)
OAuth as the sole authorization method and all API calls using the listing's public app ID / client ID
Live, public setup guide, install button URL, support resource URLs, Terms of Service URL, and Privacy Policy URL (each under 250 characters, crawlable by HubSpot Crawler)
A shared-data table that matches the requested scopes (read+write object scopes advertised as bi-directional)
Pricing that matches your website; free plans only for free-forever or freemium
Agreement to the Technology Partner Program Agreement and compliance with HubSpot branding/trademark rules
For certification: 60 active installs, 95% success rate over 30 days, demo video showing disconnect + Uninstall App endpoint, verified domain, security assessment and questionnaire
commonRejections: Fewer than 3 active unaffiliated installs, or installs that are only test accounts
Requesting scopes the app does not use, or requesting sensitive / highly_sensitive data scopes
Dead or non-public listing URLs (HubSpot verifies every URL with its crawler)
Overlapping functionality with an existing listing from the same developer instead of updating it
Use of classic CRM cards, an unsupported platform version, or a legacy app type
A second app submitted while another is still under review (auto-rejected)
Combining the HubSpot name or sprocket with your app name or logo
Certification only: API success rate below 95%, often from unthrottled 429s or one-at-a-time contact fetches instead of batch endpoints

nuances.title: Legacy public apps are gone; projects are mandatory
nuances.detail: Since June 23, 2026 you cannot create a legacy public app in the UI; new apps are CLI projects on platform version 2026.09 (2026.03 and 2025.2 still accepted). Legacy private app creation was also disabled (Aug 27, 2026) in favor of Service Keys, and HubSpot has announced v1-v3 APIs plus legacy public/private apps go unsupported in September 2027.

nuances.title: Access tokens live 30 minutes
nuances.detail: expires_in is 1800 seconds. You must store the refresh token and refresh proactively; HubSpot does not document a refresh-token expiry, and community experience is that it stays valid until the app is uninstalled or the token is deleted (unverified).

nuances.title: Required vs optional scopes decide whether an install succeeds
nuances.detail: If the portal's tier lacks a scope in requiredScopes (or a conditionallyRequiredScopes entry you put in the scope param) the install errors out for the user. Optional scopes are dropped silently; the token's scope list is the only source of truth. Common pattern: ship two install URLs, one with the tier-gated scope and one without.

nuances.title: Rate limit: 110 requests per 10 seconds per installed portal
nuances.detail: Publicly distributed OAuth apps get 110 requests / 10 s per installing account (HubSpot's current number; older docs said 100). The CRM Search API is excluded and has its own limits; the API Limit Increase add-on does not raise OAuth limits. Private/static apps instead get 100 (Free/Starter) or 190 (Pro/Enterprise) per 10 s plus a shared daily cap of 250k/625k/1M. Exceeding returns 429 and Marketplace apps must keep errors under 5% daily.

nuances.title: Redirect URL rules
nuances.detail: HTTPS only in production, http://localhost permitted for testing, must be a domain (no IP addresses), multiple URLs allowed, and the redirect_uri in the authorize request must match one declared in app-hsmeta.json redirectUrls. For Composio, register https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback.

nuances.title: Install requires a Super Admin and shows an unverified-app warning
nuances.detail: Only Super Admins or users with Marketplace Access permission can install. Until you verify your domain via DNS TXT record (one per account, up to 48 h propagation) or get listed on the Marketplace, installers see an unverified-app warning they must acknowledge.

nuances.title: Tokens reflect app scopes, not user permissions
nuances.detail: A user restricted to owned contacts who installs an app with crm.objects.contacts.read gives the app all contacts. Platform version 2026.09 adds user-level access for apps, which Marketplace AI-connector apps must adopt.

nuances.title: Test accounts emulate Enterprise and expire
nuances.detail: Developer test accounts get a 90-day Enterprise trial and are deleted after 90 days without API calls. Because they are Enterprise, they will not reproduce the scope-gating failures a Starter customer will hit; use the Customize my test account tier picker.

blockers.blocker: You need to install into a customer's Starter/Pro portal but your app lists a tier-gated scope (automation, content, custom objects) as required, so every install fails.
blockers.workaround: Move the scope to optionalScopes or conditionallyRequiredScopes in app-hsmeta.json, re-run hs project upload, and branch your code on the scopes actually present in the token.

blockers.blocker: The hs CLI needs hs account auth, which requires an interactive browser login to generate a personal access key, so a headless agent cannot bootstrap alone.
blockers.workaround: Have the human run hs account auth once (or paste the personal access key); the agent can then run every project create/upload/open command non-interactively. Alternatively use Composio-managed HUBSPOT auth and skip app creation.

blockers.blocker: You only want API access to one portal and do not want to run an OAuth server.
blockers.workaround: Create the project with distribution private and auth.type static (single-account install with a static token) or, in 2026.09, a Service Key. Note legacy private apps cannot be newly created from the UI since Aug 2026.

blockers.blocker: Marketplace listing requires 3 active unaffiliated installs before you can be listed, a chicken-and-egg problem for a new app.
blockers.workaround: Distribute first via the install URL to design partners (allowlisted OAuth distribution needs no review), accumulate 3 production installs with activity in the last 30 days, then submit the listing.

blockers.blocker: Hitting 429s at 110 requests per 10 seconds per portal when syncing large CRMs.
blockers.workaround: Use batch endpoints (batch read/create up to 100 records), the CRM Search API (separate limit), and webhook subscriptions for change detection; back off on X-HubSpot-RateLimit-Remaining. The paid API add-on does not raise OAuth limits.

blockers.blocker: Domain verification requires DNS access the developer may not have, and without it installers see an unverified-app warning.
blockers.workaround: Ask the domain owner to add the TXT record (up to 48 h), or accept the warning for internal/allowlisted installs; Marketplace-listed apps are exempt.

agentDoes: Install the HubSpot CLI, run hs project create, and author hsproject.json / app-hsmeta.json with OAuth auth, redirectUrls (including the Composio callback if relevant), and a least-privilege scope split into required/optional/conditional.
Run hs project upload and hs project open, read the Client ID/secret from the Auth tab, and wire them into the OAuth server or Composio auth config.
Generate the install URL with the correct scope / optional_scope parameters and implement the /oauth/v3/token exchange plus 30-minute refresh loop.
Write the Marketplace listing copy, shared-data table, and scope justification; draft the certification demo-video script and security questionnaire answers.
Monitor rate-limit headers and switch to batch/search endpoints when approaching 110 req / 10 s.
humanDoes: Sign in to HubSpot as Super Admin and run hs account auth (interactive personal access key generation).
Click Connect app on the consent screen for each portal install and acknowledge the unverified-app warning.
Add the DNS TXT record for domain verification.
Accept the Technology Partner Program Agreement and submit the Marketplace listing; respond to Ecosystem Quality feedback.
Recruit the 3 (listing) or 60 (certification) real customer installs and record the uninstall-flow demo video.

Opened the developer-platform app configuration, create-an-app, working-with-oauth, scopes, legacy overview, migration, account-types, listing requirements, app-partner set-up, and certification pages and confirmed field names (redirectUrls, requiredScopes, optionalScopes, conditionallyRequiredScopes, distribution) and the 3/60 install thresholds.
Opened the HubSpot changelog and confirmed the Aug 27, 2026 legacy private app creation notice and Sep 15, 2026 legacy unsupported-by-September-2027 notice.
Opened docs.composio.dev/toolkits/managed-auth and confirmed HubSpot appears in the Composio-managed list; opened the custom auth config page and confirmed the callback URI.
unverified: Refresh-token lifetime: HubSpot docs do not state one; the claim that refresh tokens persist until uninstall is community knowledge, not confirmed on an official page read here.
The older 100 req / 10 s figure for OAuth apps: current docs say 110; I did not find the page that changed it.
Community-observed Marketplace review turnaround of 1-3 weeks is anecdotal; only the official 10-business-day / 60-day bounds are documented.

The developer-platform OAuth guide at /build-apps/authentication/oauth redirected to a login page; token lifetime for /oauth/v3/token was taken from the legacy quickstart (same 30-minute value assumed).
Whether the new 2026.09 user-level access changes the Super-Admin-only install requirement was not confirmed.
